records.name: Paraiba
records.summary:
For a trans visitor the documented signal in Paraíba is exposure, not law: the dossiers' consistent victim profile — young, Black, poor, 97% travestis and trans women, most killings in public spaces at night and outside state capitals, frequently mis-recorded by authorities — concentrates risk on people who present visibly in public. The jurisdiction recorded 4 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, mid-pack in the dossier's state ranking, within a national total of 80.

No jurisdiction-specific statute, ordinance or enforcement policy affecting trans people was found in the audited sources; the national framework applies uniformly.

sources.summary: SBT News (26 Jan 2026): ANTRA 2025 dossier — Paraíba recorded 4 trans killings in 2025, mid-pack (tied with Paraná, Rio Grande do Norte, São Paulo); Brazil total 80. Supports the record's state tally.

CNN Brasil (2024 dossier): Paraíba recorded 5 trans killings in 2024; Rio Grande do Norte, Acre and Roraima zero; Bahia, Mato Grosso and Pernambuco 8 each. Earlier-year comparison for the record's mid-pack framing.

records.name: Minas Gerais
records.summary:
For a visitor the risk in Minas Gerais is violence-exposure, patterned over two years: the jurisdiction ranked 2nd nationally in 2024 with 12 killings and tied for the top in 2025 with 8; the consistency of appearing in the top two every year signals a structurally elevated environment. Against a population of ~21 million, the 2025 rate of ~0.38/million sits at the national average, but the pattern — not the rate alone — is the distinguishing risk factor.

The 68%-outside-capitals finding of the 2024 dossier implies added danger away from the capital for a visibly trans visitor moving through the interior. No state-specific legal restriction or unique ordinance was identified; the national framework applies.

sources.summary: Sergipe em Debate / ANTRA 2024 dossier (27 Jan 2025): Minas Gerais ranked 2nd nationally with 12 trans killings in 2024 (São Paulo 16, Ceará 11); 2017-2024 cumulative MG 100. Supports the record's 2024 ranking.
SBT News (26 Jan 2026): ANTRA 2025 dossier — Minas Gerais tied 1st with Ceará at 8 trans killings in 2025; national total 80. Supports the record's 2025 tie figure.

records.name: Pernambuco
records.summary:
For a trans visitor the risk in Pernambuco is violence-exposure concentrated in the interior: the jurisdiction recorded 7 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, behind only the two 8-count units in the dossier's ranking of that year's 80 national killings. Roughly two-thirds of such killings happen in interior cities rather than state capitals, where monitoring, denunciation and access to public policy are weaker — so a visibly trans visitor in mid-sized and interior municipalities is in the geography where the recorded danger actually concentrates, alongside a victim profile of young (majority 18–29), overwhelmingly Black (70% of those recorded) travestis and trans women.

No jurisdiction-specific legal restriction or ordinance was identified in the audited sources; the national framework applies uniformly.

sources.summary: SBT News (26 Jan 2026): ANTRA 2025 dossier — Pernambuco recorded 7 trans killings in 2025, behind only the 8-count states (Ceará, Minas Gerais); Brazil total 80. Supports the record's tally.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (404; the date segment in the seed URL is dash-separated and does not resolve); the dossier cites this Valor Internacional report (27 Jan 2026) as a second source for the 2025 state-level killing counts behind the Ceará/Minas Gerais pair.

Diario de Pernambuco, Jan. 27, 2026: Pernambuco was the second Brazilian state with the most killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, with 7 homicides, per the ANTRA dossier released on Jan. 26 — the state's lowest annual count since 2022 (13), after 9 in 2023 and 8 in 2024. The dossier counts 80 trans people killed nationally in 2025, 349 killings across the Northeast from 2017 to 2025, and 83 violent deaths of trans people in Pernambuco over six years, 6th-most in the national ranking for that period. For this record: a Pernambuco-specific confirmation of the state's 2025 total and a year-by-year series showing its repeated high ranking.

G1 Caruaru e Região, Oct. 3, 2025: a trans woman was shot dead inside her home on Oct. 2, 2025 in Belo Jardim, in the Agreste interior of Pernambuco, and the Civil Police opened an inquiry to identify the author and motive, with no arrests reported at publication. The report recalls the national ANTRA count of 122 trans people killed in Brazil in 2024. For this record: a documented 2025 killing outside the Recife capital region, consistent with the dossier finding that most such killings occur in interior municipalities.

Alma Preta, July 7, 2021: Fabiana da Silva Lucas, a 30-year-old Black trans woman, was found dead on the morning of that day along highway PE-160 in Santa Cruz do Capibaribe, in the Agreste of Pernambuco, killed by several knife strikes; it was the state's third recorded case of killed trans or travesti people that month. Pernambuco's Civil Police told press the suspect, a 22-year-old known as 'Gaúcho', was lynched by locals at the scene. For this record: a documented interior-state killing of a Black travesti matching the victim profile and geography described in the summary.

records.name: Bahia
records.summary:
For a visibly trans visitor to Bahia the operative fact is persistence rather than any local legal regime: the jurisdiction appears in the top-ranked band of consecutive annual dossiers, recording 7 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025 among that year's 80 national killings. The consistent victim profile — 97% travestis and trans women, majority aged 18–29, 70% Black among racially identified cases, most killings outside state capitals — describes who carries the risk; the high absolute toll is diluted by size rather than eliminated by it.

No jurisdiction-specific ordinance or statutory restriction was identified in the audited sources; the national framework applies uniformly.

sources.summary: SBT News (26 Jan 2026): ANTRA 2025 dossier — Bahia recorded 7 trans killings in 2025, second tier behind the 8-count states; among 1,261 killings 2017-2025 Bahia is 3rd with 97 (São Paulo 151, Ceará 107). Supports the record's tally.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (404; the date segment in the seed URL is dash-separated and does not resolve); the dossier cites this Valor Internacional report (27 Jan 2026) as a second source for the 2025 state-level killing counts behind the Ceará/Minas Gerais pair.

G1 Bahia, Dec. 9, 2025: police are investigating as feminicide the killing of Rhianna, an 18-year-old trans woman, choked to death in Luís Eduardo Magalhães, in the west of Bahia, on the weekend of Dec. 6-7. The suspect, a 19-year-old app driver, drove the victim's body to the police station himself and was released after confessing and claiming self-defence; the Civil Police confirmed the feminicide investigation. For this record: a documented killing in Bahia framed by the state police as gender-based (feminicide) with the suspect initially released.

G1 Bahia, Jan. 27, 2023: the ANTRA dossier ranked Bahia the seventh Brazilian state most killing trans people, with 7 killings of travestis in the state in 2022, and recapped emblematic cases; Pernambuco led that year's negative ranking nationally. For this record: documents Bahia's appearance in the top-ranked band of consecutive annual dossiers, grounding the summary's persistence finding across years.

records.name: Goias
records.summary:
Goiás recorded 5 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025 — a per-capita rate of about 0.69 per million per year against a population of ~7.2 million, roughly 1.8 times the national rate from that year's 80 national killings. For a trans visitor the operative risk factor is geographic: the national dossier finds most such killings occur in interior cities outside the capitals, where monitoring, reporting and access to public policy are weaker, and a visitor travelling beyond the capital shares that interior exposure.

No Goiás-specific ordinance, legal restriction or protection measure was identified in the audited sources; the risk profile therefore rests on the above-national per-capita killing count and the interior-concentration pattern rather than on any local legal hostility.

sources.summary: SBT News (26 Jan 2026) reports ANTRA's 9th annual dossier: 80 trans and travesti people killed in Brazil in 2025, a ~34% fall year-on-year, Brazil first in world rankings; victims overwhelmingly travestis and trans women, killed with extreme violence. National dossier — the table behind this record's 2025 state count. Supplies this record's 2025 count (5 of 80).

Sergipe Em Debate (27 Jan 2025): ANTRA's previous-year dossier recorded 122 trans and travesti killings in Brazil in 2024, 16% below 2023, five of the victims rights defenders. Companion dossier this record cites for its 2024 comparison year.

records.name: Maranhao
records.summary:
Maranhão recorded 5 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, the same count the association dossier logged for it in 2024, so its position in the ranking's middle-upper band is persistent rather than a one-year spike. For a trans visitor the documented risk is structural exposure: two consecutive years of above-median lethal counts, a national victim profile concentrated in public places at night, and no local legal change either way.

No Maranhão-specific statute, ordinance or enforcement policy affecting trans people is documented in the audited sources; the national law applies uniformly, leaving no local legal hostility to weigh and no local protection beyond the national framework.

sources.summary: SBT News (26 Jan 2026) reports ANTRA's 9th annual dossier: 80 trans and travesti people killed in Brazil in 2025, a ~34% fall year-on-year, Brazil first in world rankings; victims overwhelmingly travestis and trans women, killed with extreme violence. National dossier — the table behind this record's 2025 state count. Supplies this record's 2025 count (5 of 80).

CNN Brasil (27 Jan 2025) on ANTRA's 2024 dossier: Brazil led world trans-killings rankings for a 16th consecutive year with 122 killed in 2024 (16% below 2023); victims mostly young, Black women, many from the Northeast; crimes marked by extreme violence. Source behind this record's 2024 count and its year-over-year comparison.
